when: goal is benchmark or convergence study
full matrix exponentiation is tractable
user needs reference accuracy
avoid: Presenting exact evolution as a scalable quantum algorithm
rationale: Exact evolution is appropriate as a classical reference and avoids product-formula error.

when: Hamiltonian is local or sparse
depth budget is strict
task is exploratory or baseline simulation
accuracy target is low or moderate
avoid: Using a single unvalidated step count for final accuracy claims
rationale: First-order Trotterization has the lowest per-step circuit cost but slower convergence.

when: Hamiltonian is decomposable into terms
first-order error is unacceptable
depth budget is moderate or relaxed
accuracy target is moderate or high

parameters.steps: sweep until observable or state error converges

avoid: Assuming second order is enough for strongly non-commuting dense Hamiltonians
rationale: Second-order symmetric product formulas reduce leading error terms at higher per-step cost.

when: Hamiltonian is decomposable into weighted terms
Hamiltonian has many terms or deterministic term traversal is expensive
randomized product-formula sampling is acceptable
task can tolerate convergence sweeps over sample count or repeated seeds

parameters.samples: sweep sample count until observable or state error converges

avoid: Treating one sampled unitary as a deterministic final answer
Ignoring stochastic variance in observable estimates
Assuming term-count independence removes dependence on total Hamiltonian weight
rationale: qDRIFT samples terms according to weights and can avoid deterministic traversal over every Hamiltonian term, making it a useful executable randomized baseline for large-term Hamiltonians.

when: domain is quantum chemistry
task involves VQE-UCCSD or QPE full-CI
property constraints include size consistency or orbital invariance

parameters.steps: benchmark against exact where tractable and test decomposition choices

avoid: Ignoring orbital localization and decomposition order
rationale: Quantum chemistry applications can expose size-consistency and orbital-invariance issues under Trotterization.

when: Hamiltonian has a dominant exactly or cheaply simulable reference component
Hamiltonian is time independent
direct Trotter depth is impractical
a dense small-system numerical reference is acceptable

parameters.steps: start with a convergence sweep; validate the selected reference split

avoid: Treating this dense reference as an interaction-picture circuit, LCU method, or asymptotic resource estimate
Using the automatic diagonal reference split without checking its suitability
rationale: OpenQEvo provides an executable dense midpoint interaction-picture reference for a split H = H0 + V.
For canonical Pauli input, diagonal I/Z terms define H0 by default; callers can select reference term indices explicitly.
Trotter and qDRIFT remain useful executable baselines when no useful reference split is available.

when: backend is noisy simulator or quantum hardware
task reports measured observables or state fidelity
base evolution circuit is available
avoid: Treating error mitigation as a standalone evolution strategy
Using mitigation to compensate for unvalidated algorithmic Trotter error
rationale: Noisy backend execution can benefit from mitigation wrappers, but the base evolution strategy and its algorithmic error must still be selected and validated separately.

when: Hamiltonian is static and Hermitian
A full dense small-system reference is tractable
Goal is approximation comparison rather than quantum subspace diagonalization

parameters.krylov_dim: sweep subspace dimension up to the Hilbert-space dimension
parameters.tolerance: choose a positive Lanczos-breakdown tolerance; not an output error guarantee

avoid: Claiming quantum state preparation, measurements, circuits, sparse scaling, or hardware advantage
Assuming an assembled approximate propagator is exactly unitary
rationale: The registered method is a dense classical reference; compare against exact and inspect approximation and unitarity errors.

when: Goal is closed-system evolution along a linear driver-to-target Hamiltonian path
Dense small-system propagation is tractable
A linear schedule and the selected initial driver model are suitable

parameters.steps: sweep positive step counts for midpoint convergence
parameters.initial_hamiltonian: supply a compatible driver or explicitly accept the default transverse-field driver

avoid: Treating finite-time propagation as proof of adiabaticity or a ground-state guarantee
Claiming analog hardware, open-system dynamics, spectral-gap estimates, or optimization performance
rationale: The API propagates a linear Hamiltonian path; adiabatic state following also requires an appropriate initial state, total time, and gap/schedule assessment.

when: Goal is dense closed-system evolution along a linear or positive-power Hamiltonian interpolation
Explicit initial and final Hermitian matrix terms with matching dimensions are available
Full dense propagation is tractable

parameters.initial_terms: supply initial dense Hermitian matrices matching the final terms
parameters.schedule: choose linear or a supported power schedule with finite positive exponent

avoid: Passing a canonical Pauli object to this dense-matrix-only API
Interpreting propagation as a gap calculation, adiabatic guarantee, or hardware annealing workflow
rationale: The separate dense adiabatic_evolution API accepts initial_terms and linear/power schedules; it does not choose a runtime or initialize a ground state.
